title: Interest on Late Dental Tier-Difference Credits — Premium Billing Accounts
content:
**Rule.** Interest is added to the dental tier-difference credit on a Premium Billing Accounts arrangement when the drop is credited late. It is added after any deduction and after the floor at 0.00; the credit is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

| Days from the departed dependent's termination date to the credit date | Interest added |
|---|---|
| more than 90 | 15 percent a year of the lag interest base |
| more than 30, up to and including 90 | 10 percent a year of the lag interest base |
| 30 or fewer | none |

**The lag interest base** is the tier difference per month reduced by the prepay discount percentage (4 percent on Cascade Individual Annual Prepay, 0 percent on every other arrangement), for each prepaid month after the dependent's termination date that is not among the months already credited — counted as the whole calendar months from that termination date to the paid-through date less the months already credited, never fewer than zero, and zero where no paid-through date is on record — running for the days from that termination date to the credit date beyond 30, on an actual-days basis over 365. In words: that discounted monthly difference, multiplied by those months, multiplied by the days beyond 30, divided by 365.

The tier difference per month is the subscriber's Dental PPO Plans plan's monthly premium for the tier billed before the drop (the departed dependent's recorded tier) less its monthly premium for the tier after the drop (the subscriber's active enrollment's tier), never less than zero. It is zero where no departed dependent or no active subscriber enrollment is on record. The months already credited are the months covered by plan-change difference credits on the dental line booked since the departed dependent's termination month; a credit counts as booked since that month when the whole calendar months from its booking date to the credit date are no more than the whole calendar months from the dependent's termination date to the credit date. Whole calendar months are counted the way an anniversary is counted: a month is complete only when a later month reaches the same day number, and the last day of a shorter month does not complete it.

**Boundary points.** 30 days: none. 31 days: 10 percent. 90 days: 10 percent. 91 days: 15 percent.

**Worked example (hypothetical).** Annual Prepay; tier difference 48.55, so 46.608 after 4 percent; termination 31 May; paid through 31 December, 7 whole months; none already credited; credit date 20 August, 81 days after termination. Base: 46.608 multiplied by 7, multiplied by 51, divided by 365, about 45.586. 81 days is more than 30 and not more than 90, so interest is 10 percent: about 4.5586.
